No, it does not use a database transaction. According to [[concepts/write-journal]], the system achieves atomic write semantics **without** needing an actual database transaction — the journal itself serves as the transaction log, kept in memory for the duration of a single run.

The rollback happens purely through the in-memory write journal: before any file is overwritten, the prior state is recorded, and if a run fails, the journal can roll back every recorded write in reverse order by restoring previous file content or deleting newly created files.
